checkpoints.description: Task 'task-pebble-v8-text-predicates' completed successfully.

[1/4] Plan: add one numeric list builtin, sum(values), accepting ints and floats like min/max, returning int for an all-int list, refusing bools and non-numbers, and applying the existing int-digit and finite-float caps to the result; ADR-014 and failing-first tests first

impact_assessment.why: Pebble can order a list and take its extremes but cannot total it, so every score, size or cost total is a hand-written accumulator loop, which is the one numeric list operation scripts still write by hand.
impact_assessment.benefits: Scripts total a list in one call and keep the int/float distinction the rest of the language already uses, with the same caps that protect int and float arithmetic.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: surface grows to 23 builtins and ADR-002's list is amended; dependency: none, standard library only; concurrency: none, single-threaded interpreter; state: no files or schemas change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-014 pins the empty-list result, the int/float promotion, the bool refusal and the two result caps before code; failing-first tests including a patched-cap test; full aikit check pebble gate.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] sum is green: int totals stay int, a float value promotes the result, empty list is 0, bool/non-number elements are refused with their index, and both result caps apply (patched MAX_INT_BITS test and a finite-float test); 7 new tests, full suite 232 green

[3/4] Docs: ADR-014 records sum, its int/float promotion and both result caps; README lists twenty-three builtins and 232 tests plus examples/totals.peb; codebase map regenerated; aikit check pebble 4/4 gates green; checklists: passed
Task 'task-pebble-v9-sum' completed successfully.

[1/4] Plan: a deterministic crash-fuzz guard under ADR-015 with four corpora (token soup, typed structured programs, every example, single-token mutations) and a CLI-shield check, all with patched resource caps, plus a floor on successful runs so the corpus cannot silently degrade

impact_assessment.why: ADR-001 and ADR-003 promise every program failure is a positioned Pebble report, and that promise is tested only by hand-written cases; a regression that lets a host exception escape a new builtin would pass the suite.
impact_assessment.benefits: One seeded corpus exercises lexer, parser, evaluator and the CLI shield together, so a crash is reproducible from a seed and a printed sample rather than reported by a user.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no language surface change, only test coverage; dependency: none, standard library random only; concurrency: none; state: no files or schemas change; timing: the whole fuzz module must stay far below the test budget.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Fixed seed, patched caps so a hostile sample stays cheap, a minimum-success floor, and a measured 41ms module runtime; full aikit check pebble gate.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Fuzz module is green: seeded token soup, typed structured corpus (89/120 runs succeed, floor 60), every example at real and reduced caps, 60 mutated examples, and the CLI-shield check; one classify helper avoids silent excepts, hygiene and guidelines gates pass; 238 tests, fuzz module 48ms

[3/4] Docs: ADR-015 records the seeded crash-fuzz guard and its costs; README adds test_fuzz.py to the tree, a fuzz run command, and the v10 status at 238 tests; codebase map regenerated; aikit check pebble 4/4 gates green; checklists: passed
Task 'task-pebble-v10-crash-fuzz' completed successfully.

[1/4] Plan: add average(values) under ADR-016, the follow-up ADR-014 named: a float result for any non-empty number list, an error for an empty list because there is no average of nothing, and the same element and finiteness rules sum already enforces

impact_assessment.why: ADR-014 gave lists a total and deliberately deferred an average because it needs a zero-length rule; that rule is a one-line contract, and until it exists every script writes sum(xs) / len(xs) and must remember to guard an empty list itself.
impact_assessment.benefits: Scripts get a mean in one call with a stated empty-list behaviour, composing with sum, sort and the text helpers to turn parsed fields into statistics.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: surface grows to 24 builtins and ADR-002's list is amended; dependency: none, standard library only; concurrency: none, single-threaded interpreter; state: no files or schemas change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-016 pins the empty-list error, the always-float result and the finiteness guard before code; failing-first tests including both guards; full aikit check pebble gate.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] average is green: always-float mean, empty list is a positioned error, shared _numbers element rule now used by sum too, and a guarded division so an int inside the digit cap but beyond float range reports instead of raising OverflowError; the fuzz corpus now includes 10 ^ 3990; 8 new tests, 245 total

[3/4] Docs: ADR-016 records average, its empty-list error and the guarded division; README lists twenty-four builtins and 245 tests, examples/totals.peb shows both means; codebase map regenerated; aikit check pebble 4/4 gates green; checklists: passed
Task 'task-pebble-v11-average' completed successfully.

[1/5] Plan: add round(value) and round(value, digits) under ADR-017, choosing decimal half-up (away from zero on ties) over the host's banker's rounding, capping digits at 0..15 and refusing bools, non-finite values and a non-int digit count; failing-first tests first

impact_assessment.why: Pebble can total, average, floor and take absolute values but cannot round, so every formatted number needs floor(x + 0.5) written by hand, which silently gives the wrong sign for negatives and cannot round to a decimal place at all.
impact_assessment.benefits: Scripts round to a whole number or to a stated number of decimal places with one rule, and the tie behaviour is stated in an ADR rather than inherited from a host default that surprises users.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: surface grows to 25 builtins and ADR-002's list is amended, and round(x) returns an int while round(x, d) returns a float; dependency: decimal from the standard library; concurrency: none; state: no files or schema changes.
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-017 pins half-up ties, the digit range, the int/float result split and the non-finite guard before code; failing-first tests for ties, negatives, digits and guards; fuzz corpus extended; full aikit check pebble gate.

checkpoints.description: [2/5] round is green: decimal half-up ties away from zero, int result for one argument and float for a digit count, 0..15 digit range, bool/non-number/non-finite refusals, and huge ints handled without a decimal InvalidOperation (whole numbers return exactly, digit counts report a float overflow); fuzz corpus includes round; 7 new tests, 252 total

[3/5] Docs: ADR-017 records round, the half-up tie rule, the int/float result split, the 0..15 digit range and the decimal-over-IEEE choice; README lists twenty-five builtins and 252 tests with a round example; examples/totals.peb rounds an average both ways; codebase map regenerated; aikit check pebble 4/4 gates green; checklists: passed
Task 'task-pebble-v12-round' completed successfully.

[1/5] Plan: add index_of(list, value) and extend contains to lists under ADR-018, moving Pebble equality into formatting.py so the evaluator and the builtins share one rule; failing-first tests first, including cross-type and nested-list cases

impact_assessment.why: Pebble can search text and order a list but cannot ask whether a list holds a value or where, so every membership check is a hand-written for loop with a found flag and a position variable.
impact_assessment.benefits: Scripts check and locate list members in one call, and equality is stated once for ==, contains and index_of instead of a second definition growing in the stdlib.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: surface grows to 26 builtins, contains gains a list form that amends ADR-012, and equality moves modules; dependency: none, standard library only; concurrency: none; state: no files or schema changes.
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-018 pins that both builtins use the same equality as ==, that index_of returns none for a miss, and that a non-list first argument to the list form is a positioned error; failing-first tests; fuzz corpus extended; full aikit check pebble gate.

checkpoints.description: [2/5] index_of and the list form of contains are green: both compare with formatting.values_equal, so == and the builtins share one rule (numbers mix, bools do not, nested lists deep, other kinds never); index_of returns none on a miss; 11 new tests, 263 total

[3/5] Docs: ADR-018 records index_of, the list form of contains and the move of Pebble equality to formatting.values_equal; README lists twenty-six builtins and 263 tests, examples/sorted.peb searches a list; the fuzz corpus generates index_of and list contains; codebase map regenerated; aikit check pebble 4/4 gates green; checklists: passed
